title: openai-compat: map tool schemas + unify tool_choice semantics and tool message formatting
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: customers using the OpenAI-compatible API expect function/tool calling semantics (tool schemas, tool_choice events, and tool-formatted messages) to match OpenAI behavior closely. We observed two incompatibilities: 1) tool schemas were not consistently mapped to Redwood's internal ToolDefinition schema (leading to missing required fields for some generator clients), and 2) the tool_choice + tool message formatting returned by the runtime differed from OpenAI's expected structure, which broke downstream SDKs and streaming clients.

Summary: This PR implements a compatibility layer that: (a) maps OpenAI-style tool schemas (parameters/required/properties) to Redwood ToolDefinition during request ingestion; (b) adds explicit tool_choice semantics in the chat generation pipeline so the first tool choice emitted is tagged and surfaced exactly like OpenAI (tool_choice event with name + reason); and (c) standardizes tool message formatting so tool call outputs are emitted as a tool message with content that contains the original JSON payload under a single text block plus a metadata header for provenance.

Changes: high-level commits and rationale are included below. The description includes a short checklist and compatibility notes for SDKs and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] schema mapping: parameters -> tool.parameters, required -> tool.required, property types normalized
- [x] tool_choice event: emit on first tool selection, include reason field matching OpenAI semantics
- [x] tool message formatting: single content block with JSON payload and provenance header
- [x] unit and integration tests for streaming and non-streaming flows
- [x] docs updates for OpenAI compatibility table and example flows

Compatibility notes:
- The mapping is best-effort: unsupported JSON Schema keywords (e.g. "unevaluatedProperties") are ignored with a warning logged and surfaced to the SDK as a warning in the compatibility report.
- ToolChoice semantics: we follow OpenAI practice of preferring tool selection events over inline tool instructions when the model emits a tool_choice token sequence. The runtime now converts its internal selection to the OpenAI-style event when the request uses the openai-compat header.

Example formatting (OpenAI-compatible):
- Tool call event emitted to client: {
  "type": "tool_call",
  "tool": "weather_lookup",
  "arguments": "{"location": "San Francisco"}",
  "id": "call-123"
}
- Tool message delivered as a chat message from "tool:weather_lookup":
  Content (text): "-- REDWOOD-TOOL-JSON --
{"temp_c": 14, "conditions": "Partly Cloudy"}
-- END --"

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/openai_compat/schema_mapper.py: map OpenAI schemas -> Redwood ToolDefinition, add compatibility warnings
- runtime/openai_compat/tool_choice.py: canonicalize tool_choice events and integrate with streaming hooks
- runtime/streaming/formatter.py: standardize tool message content block + provenance header
- sdk/python/openai_compat_examples.md: docs and examples for tool calling and streaming clients
- tests/integration/test_tool_call_streaming.py: added coverage for streaming tool calls and replays

Testing and CI: All unit tests and integration tests were run in CI. Integration tests initially flaked on a timing edge in the streaming harness; I reproduced locally and added a small debounce + test stabilization change in streaming/transport to avoid flakes. CI rerun passed.

Merge notes: Squash-merged to main after approvals. No runtime config flags required; compatibility is opt-in via the request header or a per-route setting in the console.

Related work: PRs pr-35712 (openai compat initial tool-calling), pr-41567 (tool-choice semantics discussion), and ENG-4821 (project to improve compatibility).
